report.title: NCCL_IB_HCA Config Collapse Incident
report.summary: The cluster training job degraded to 75% throughput due to a launcher config change (v43) that pinned NCCL_IB_HCA to a single interface (mlx5_0), collapsing 8 InfiniBand rails into one and saturating bandwidth at ~396 Gb/s. The published revert did not affect the running job since NCCL_IB_HCA is read at startup. A restart with v42 was required to restore all 8 rails and achieve 100.2% baseline throughput.
report.root_cause: Launcher config v43 set NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0 cluster-wide, collapsing 8 IB rails to one. The running job retained v43 settings because NCCL_IB_HCA is read at process startup and cannot be changed on a running job. The published revert_rollout did not propagate to the active training instance.
report.proof: counterfactual: removing [{"kind": "comm"}] explains 96.6% of the slowdown; rank_timings show comm wait 2.11s vs p50 0.62s uniform across all ranks; network_status shows one NIC at 396.3 Gb/s with 448/512 idle; change_log confirms v43 diff NCCL_IB_HCA all 8 rails -> mlx5_0.
report.fix: Revert published launcher config to v42 and restart the training job. The config revert restores NCCL_IB_HCA to all 8 interfaces (mlx5_0..mlx5_7). The restart is required because NCCL_IB_HCA is read at startup and cannot be modified on a running job.
report.verification: 200 steps 02:55:12Z-03:09:57Z: 473.5k tok/s = 100.2% of baseline, step p50 4.40s p95 4.45s, new error lines on in-job nodes: 0, loss trend normal -> PASS

runbook.fix: 1. Revert launcher config to v42 (restores NCCL_IB_HCA to all 8 IB rails). 2. Restart the training job so it picks up v42 at startup. This is the disruptive action requiring human approval.
runbook.pitfalls: NCCL_IB_HCA is read at NCCL init; cannot be changed on a running job. A simple config update without restart will have no effect. Ensure all in-flight jobs are quiesced or restarted after config revert.

report.title: Resolved: Synchronous ALLREDUCE Hang Due to GPU Hardware Failure
report.summary: A single GPU (np-9addff51-21 gpu6) failed with XID 79, causing rank 166 to stop sending heartbeats and stall the entire ALLREDUCE across all 512 GPUs. The job was safely unblocked by draining the faulty node and using a hot spare.
report.root_cause: GPU hardware failure (XID 79) on node np-9addff51-21, GPU 6, causing rank 166 to hang and block synchronous ALLREDUCE.
report.proof: Rank 166 on np-9addff51-21 gpu6 showed no heartbeat and was confirmed by kernel XID log 'GPU has fallen off the bus' and DCGM unresponsiveness, with no network or process issues.
report.fix: Drain node np-9addff51-21 to remove the dead GPU/rank, allowing the job to restart with hot spare np-9addff51-65, which restored ALLREDUCE progress.
report.verification: Post-fix, 200 steps completed at 100.3% of baseline throughput with normal latency and zero new errors, confirming successful recovery.

report.title: eval-sweep-7 Storage Contention on /mnt/datasets
report.summary: The research-evals job eval-sweep-7 launched at 02:18:03Z and immediately saturated the Crusoe Shared Disk at /mnt/datasets with 11.63 GB/s reads, starving the yuzu-70b-pretrain training job. This caused shared-disk read latency to spike from 1.9ms to 22.7ms and yuzu read throughput to drop from 9.42 to 2.98 GB/s, making data_wait the dominant slowdown component at 1.28s/step.
report.root_cause: eval-sweep-7 (TP=8/PP=4/DP=16) performed synchronous reads at 11.63 GB/s on the shared disk, creating a bottleneck that stalled all 512 GPUs in the training job via dataloader wait.
report.proof: counterfactual: removing [{"kind": "data_wait"}] explains 96.8% of the slowdown; storage_status confirms shared-disk read latency rose from 1.9ms to 22.7ms and yuzu throughput dropped from 9.42 to 2.98 GB/s concurrent with eval-sweep-7 launch.
report.fix: paused eval-sweep-7 immediately to remove the 11.63 GB/s shared-disk read load, restoring latency to ~1.9ms and collapsing dataloader wait.
report.verification: 200 steps from 02:27:28Z to 02:42:13Z achieved 473.9k tok/s (100.3% of baseline), step p50 4.40s p95 4.45s, and zero new error lines on in-job nodes.

The root cause was identified as storage contention, confirmed by temporal alignment, magnitude analysis, and counterfactual verification showing data_wait accounts for ~97% of the slowdown.
report.root_cause: eval-sweep-7 launched at 02:05:29Z reading /mnt/datasets at 12.87 GB/s, saturating the Crusoe Shared Disk and displacing yuzu-70b-pretrain read bandwidth from 9.36 to 2.67 GB/s with latency spiking from 2.1ms to 22.1ms.

report.fix: Enable local NVMe shard cache for yuzu-70b-pretrain pointing to /mnt/datasets/yuzu-mix-v3. This serves training data reads from node-local NVMe instead of the contended shared disk, removing the contention mechanism without restarting the job.

report.title: Degraded InfiniBand NIC on np-9addff51-21 causing 89% throughput drop
report.summary: A single degraded InfiniBand NIC (mlx5_7) on node np-9addff51-21 caused severe communication bottlenecks, reducing training throughput to 89% of baseline. The issue was confirmed by counterfactual analysis showing 95.2% of slowdown explained by removing comm, and resolved by draining the node, restoring performance to 100% of baseline.
report.root_cause: Degraded InfiniBand NIC mlx5_7 on node np-9addff51-21 with +2746 symbol errors, +4 link downs, and 57.3 GB/s bandwidth (vs 186 GB/s median), causing NCCL link-down errors and stalling synchronous training.
report.proof: Counterfactual removal of communication bottleneck explains 95.2% of slowdown; network_status shows only one NIC (mlx5_7) with new errors; explain_slowdown removing ranks 160-167 yields 0% improvement; GPU thermal and storage metrics rule out other causes.
report.fix: Drain node np-9addff51-21 to remove the degraded NIC from the training job, using the available healthy spare node np-9addff51-65.
report.verification: 200 steps from 03:05:34Z-03:20:19Z achieved 473.9k tok/s (100.3% of baseline) with p50/p95 step times of 4.40s/4.45s and zero new error lines on in-job nodes.
